    - Gorm. Master of the Stairs, eleven years. Born halfway up the Long Stair. My father cut stone for the quay walls.
    - Ulric taught me everything I know about stone. I still take him every difficult piece of rock. For a second opinion. Only ever a second opinion.
    - My father died of a fall when I was thirteen. I sat on the step outside our door all that winter and would not go anywhere.
    - Then Ulric sat down beside me, put a chisel in my hand, and said if I meant to sit on a step all day I might as well learn how it was made. I have never told the crews that. Nor will you.
    - Every step on these cliffs has a temper. The old stair above the quay is getting tired and wants looking after. The third landing is sulking. People laugh. Then they live here a few years and stop laughing.
    - And Ulric's little animals. A crab here, a hare there, a gull, a seal. I have walked past a thousand of them and I love every one.
    - I promised the First Warden a stair down to the far cove before the race, so the town can stand on the rocks and watch the boats go out. The rock is harder and more broken than it looked. A whole flight cracked in the spring frost.
    - And the crews will not work the lowest landings after dark. I am behind. I would sooner cut every step myself than say so. So I have not said so. You did not hear it.
    - Ulric is still on the Anvil, by daylight, slow as the tide. The crews work the lower flights again with someone watching the face. Behind, still. Less behind.
    - Three flights left, and a handrope Kestra strung like a fiddle. It will be done before the race. I said it to Iska and I will not unsay it.
    - Up or down, use the stairs. Not the basket.
    - Good. The crew is ready. Stone does not wait.
